overview: Canada is the second-largest country in the world by area, covering most of the northern half of North America. Its capital is Ottawa and its largest city is Toronto. Canada is a constitutional monarchy and a federation of ten provinces and three territories. English and French are both official languages, and French is the main language in the province of Quebec.

geography.text: Canada has coastlines on three oceans, the Pacific, the Atlantic and the Arctic, and the longest coastline of any country. The Rocky Mountains rise in the west, the Prairies cover the middle, and the ancient rocks of the Canadian Shield, dotted with lakes, cover much of the centre and east. Canada has more lakes than any other country, and most Canadians live in the south, close to the border with the United States.

history.text: Indigenous peoples have lived in Canada for thousands of years. French and British settlers arrived from the 1500s onwards, and Britain took control of New France in 1763. Canada became a self-governing confederation in 1867 and gradually gained full independence, finally bringing its constitution home from Britain in 1982.

events.title: Vikings arrive
events.text: Norse explorers build a settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland.

events.title: Quebec founded
events.text: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec City.

events.title: Britain takes New France
events.text: France gives up its North American colonies.

events.title: Confederation
events.text: Canada becomes a self-governing country within the British Empire.

events.title: Constitution Act
events.text: Canada gains full control of its constitution.

government.text: Canada is a federal constitutional monarchy. The British monarch is head of state, represented by a Governor General, and the Prime Minister leads the government with the support of the elected House of Commons. Its ten provinces and three territories have their own governments. Canada was a founding member of NATO.

economy.text: Canada has one of the world's largest economies. It is rich in natural resources: oil, natural gas, timber, minerals and fresh water. It exports cars and machinery, and most of its trade is with the United States. Services such as banking make up most jobs.

culture.text: Canada has two official languages, English and French; most French speakers live in Quebec. First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples have their own cultures and languages. Canadians gave the world basketball, the telephone (through Alexander Graham Bell's work) and poutine: fries with cheese curds and gravy.

items.title: Two languages
items.text: English and French are both official across the federal government.

items.title: Poutine
items.text: Fries, cheese curds and gravy, first served in rural Quebec.

items.title: Basketball
items.text: Invented by Canadian James Naismith in 1891.

sport.text: Ice hockey is Canada's national winter sport and lacrosse its national summer sport. Canada has won more Olympic gold medals in ice hockey than any other country. It hosted the Summer Olympics in Montreal in 1976 and the Winter Olympics in Calgary in 1988 and Vancouver in 2010, and co-hosted the 2026 World Cup.

items.title: Ice hockey
items.text: Canada's men and women have won Olympic hockey gold many times.

items.title: Wayne Gretzky
items.text: 'The Great One' holds dozens of NHL records.

About 60% of the world's lakes are in Canada.
